doc.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-10-07

title: De De as extra trumpet in other men's bands
summary: He was hired out as second trumpet to Rene, Buddy and others, and describes how the bands mixed.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Well after Arnold had passed, who were some of those other bands that you just splattered around with and stuff?

None in particular, like I said, Renee, Chris, Guy Kelly, he was with Celestine Warr, and the time he'd get work, you know. Split the band, I'd work in their place. I was mostly hired out like that. And one small orchestra, with myself, let me see Rochon, where he's living, he's preaching now.

Sax. Nice sax. I was playing with Glenny, some time. I had Gus Green too, bass. I had, what's that boy, Shelly was playing with the Glen brothers? Played piano with Simon Fraser. Mm-hmm. Piano. Right, a fellow by the name of Right, tenor sax. I think it was Walter, Henry Wright, I don't know if he's working today. In the age too, I guess. How many fellows out the game, you know. Oh yeah. I didn't turn it. Instead they out. Well what about guys like Chris and Buddy and Boots and Boots and? Who's playing with the Glen brothers? I don't know if he's working today. I don't know if he's working today. In the age too, I guess not. How many fellows out the game, you know. Oh yeah. I didn't turn it, you know. Instead they out. stuff
Well, what about guys like Chris and Buddy and... Who was that guy? Chris and Buddy and Rene and all those, would you play any second trumpet to them ever?

I have played second to Rene. I played second to Buddy too at times, you know. Most of the time, sometimes they'd split, they'd get in, they'd had so much work to it was. At that time, they'd split the band, you see. They'd send me either with the bass and they'd hire out the different ones, you know. You know, on them spot jobs, and they needed trumpet player, well they'd hire me. In fact, Rene taken the liking to me, I started playing following his, and I guess that's about what it was, you see, and I couldn't work then, you see. Every time he'd get a hold of something, and Rene sent me on his job, these fellas, see that I could have popped up a whole little. Rene's ain't part of it anyway, so at the time they needed trumpet player, they'd come to me too, you see. That's where that went.
Remember any of the guys that Rene would have in his band?
What's up? Uh, Glennie with the bass. Oh yeah? Oh yeah, ooh. That's his, that's his R's, Rene's R's. One man Glennie. His ace. Let's see.
I think Sonny Henry, I think he played trombone a lot.
I didn't know that Sonny did much orchestra work.
He did in those days. Yeah, he did, he did.

Those bands would be so mixed up sometimes, you'd see a member in one band and you'd look in another band and there'd be another band. It split up, you know, the bass and trumpet mostly stick together or a drum or something like that and outside the sax or the clarinet, like Big Al Lowy and things like that. Big Al Lowy played with René Lodge too. Louis Nelson, Louis Nelson, Louis Nelson.
Oh yeah, I knew him. I did too. I worked with him.
